key_insight: The paper replaces sample-wise rewards with distribution-wise rewards to better align generative model optimization with real data distributions and reduce reward hacking, mode collapse, and visual anomalies.
engineering_relevance: For image-generation systems, this offers a practical reinforcement-learning finetuning strategy that can improve fidelity and diversity while remaining applicable across different base models.
method: Use distribution-wise rewards instead of evaluating each generated sample independently.
Apply a subset-replace strategy to estimate rewards efficiently by updating only a small subset of a generated reference set.
Use RL to optimize post-hoc model merging coefficients to reduce train-inference inconsistency from SDE-based regularization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved FID-50K on multiple models, including SiT from 8.30 to 5.77 and EDM2 from 3.74 to 3.52, with qualitative gains in perceptual quality and diversity.
watch_item: Reward estimation and subset-replace updates may add implementation complexity, and the approach still requires careful tuning to avoid instability or overfitting to the chosen distribution metric.
paper_title: Optimizing Visual Generative Models via Distribution-wise Rewards
